patch_description:
This implementation replaces expensive simulated annealing with a deterministic coordinate-wise feasibility pump. The containing region is a fixed unit-area right triangle, so normalized minimum triangle area is invariant and can be optimized directly.

For each movable point, all triangle-area constraints involving that point become linear half-plane constraints when the other twelve points are fixed. The algorithm therefore performs repeated maximin coordinate updates: it binary-searches the greatest feasible minimum determinant and intersects the corresponding half-planes with the containing triangle. This raises bottleneck triangles directly rather than relying on stochastic acceptance of random perturbations.

Multiple deterministic randomized simplex initializations explore distinct orientation chambers, while feasibility-based local refinement is substantially faster than repeatedly recomputing convex hulls during annealing. A final scale converts the reference triangle to exactly unit area.
